final_content.statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Fix a Noetherian scheme $S$ and the category $\mathrm{FTS}_S$ of separated finite-type $S$-schemes. For $f:X\to Y$ therein, let $f^!:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_Y)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}^+(\mathcal O_X)$ be the upper-shriek functor built from the right adjoint to proper pushforward on a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\bar X\to Y$. In particular $f^!\mathcal O_Y$ is a coherent bounded complex when $f$ is perfect. Let $f:X\to Y$ be flat in $\mathrm{FTS}_S$, and $x\in X$. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) the fibre-local ring $\mathcal O_{X_{f(x)},x}$ is Cohen–Macaulay; (2) there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $x$ on which $f^!\mathcal O_Y|_U$ is quasi-isomorphic to a *single* coherent cohomology sheaf placed in one cohomological degree (the degree may depend on $U$). In particular this is a neighbourhood statement about the relative dualizing complex, not just its single stalk.
hypotheses: f flat separated finite-type between S-schemes and point x.
conclusions: CM at x iff relative upper-shriek structure complex locally has only one nonzero cohomology sheaf.
